data.description:
Split from silvern-dewy-damselfly (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) during its plan review.

## Problem

After a close whose completion-signature append failed, a LATER reader cannot tell the ticket apart from one closed with the gate off: both present as "no valid completion attestation". Damselfly makes the loss machine-readable IN THE RETURNED PAYLOAD of the call that suffered it, but that payload is ephemeral — an agent that was not the caller, or the same agent in a later session, has no durable discriminator.

## Why it was split out

Damselfly's first draft proposed a best-effort audit comment. That is unsound: the comment appends through the SAME event_append -> write_lock (60s) path whose timeout produced the SigningError, so under the contention that causes the bug the record is missing in exactly the case it exists for.

The sound mechanism is to record the EXPECTATION at close time, in the same locked write that already commits the STATUS event (src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:377 txn.transition_core, which already carries close_class and force_close_reason) — so no additional lock acquisition is needed. A reader then compares 'a completion signature was expected' against 'a valid completion attestation exists'; expected-and-absent is the lost-signature state, and gate-off reads as not-expected.

That is an EVENT-SCHEMA addition (event schema + reducer + docs/event-schema.md), which is a materially different and more cross-cutting change than damselfly's reporting fix, so it is tracked separately rather than hand-waved inside it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A close that expected a completion signature records that expectation durably in the same locked write as the STATUS event, with no additional lock acquisition
- [ ] A later reader, holding no lock, distinguishes closed-and-signed from closed-with-signature-lost from closed-with-gate-off
- [ ] The added field is versioned and documented in docs/event-schema.md, and an older reader that does not know it degrades safely
data.title: Closed-without-signature is not distinguishable from gate-off on read
